accounting.rationale: Assumed R401 gives a nonempty comma-separated list. Explicit R804/C810 govern object-name. No array-spec, coarray-spec, component-reference or bare all-items alternative is written in R834.

Normative statement-to-attribute mechanism for the listed objects. The variable category, possible operations, pending-affector obligation, scoped association and subobject effects retain 8.5.4 and its canonical owners. No duplicate local S runtime classifier is created.
The R834 statement is one explicit route permitted by 8.5.1. It is not an ASYNCHRONOUS= I/O control specifier or the initiation of communication.
PENDING exact source-use of 8.5.4p1-p4. The attribute does not require actual I/O, communication, overlap, latency, an optimization choice or a change to an ordinary printed value.

Each listed actual object receives the attribute in the appropriate scope. USE/HOST and nonlocal BLOCK identity must be retained; unlike ALLOCATABLE, an ASYNCHRONOUS statement alone need not introduce a new local/construct entity.

12.6.2.5p4 independently supplies implicit ASYNCHRONOUS in the transfer statement's scoping unit and permits explicit confirmation. Preserve 8.5.4 S owners, 12.6/12.7 and 18.10.4 operation owners, C815's explicit-duplication rule and actual caller/state restrictions; no SourceUses instance or canonical connection is authored.

requirements.title: An ASYNCHRONOUS statement has an optional double colon and a nonempty object-name list
requirements.definition: The ASYNCHRONOUS keyword is followed by an optional double colon and a nonempty comma-separated list of object names. It specifies the ASYNCHRONOUS attribute for those objects through 8.5.4, not an executable asynchronous operation. The statement supplies no array/coarray specification or type/parameter selector; those properties follow their own explicit or implicit rules. Scope identity and canonical eligibility are not waived.

pending.double-colon-form: PENDING compile/positive-control: complete ordinary program or procedure with a typed scalar INTEGER variable and one ASYNCHRONOUS :: name statement in its specification part. No I/O, pending operation, undefined-value read or effect claim is needed for syntax admission.
pending.no-double-colon-form: PENDING the otherwise equivalent complete ASYNCHRONOUS name form. Preserve source-form separation and other declaration conditions; the double colon is not mandatory.
pending.multiple-distinct-object-names: PENDING compile/positive-control: separately typed scalar and fixed-shape array variables of ordinary supported types occur once each in one comma-separated list. The statement names whole objects and does not redeclare their dimensions or require any transfer.
pending.missing-list-exclusion: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: ASYNCHRONOUS :: without a list in a complete specification part, repaired by inserting a prior-typed ordinary variable name. There is no SAVE-like listless form; exclude another valid parse and isolate this one omission.
pending.list-separator-repair: PENDING compile diagnostic/control: two existing distinct variable names with one missing or invalid list separator, repaired only to a comma. No repeated entity, duplicate explicit attribute, wrong role, malformed type or missing provider is part of the intended cause.
pending.whole-name-not-declarator-or-designator: PENDING separate compile contrasts using an array-spec suffix or percent-component designator where an object-name is required. Give the array its legitimate dimensions earlier, then delete only the suffix; for a simple derived object, delete %member to name the whole eligible parent. A coarray suffix requires a valid prior coarray declaration before its analogous repair. Do not turn an untyped or conflicting declaration into the control.
pending.implicit-io-confirmation-source-relation: PENDING canonical 12.6.2.5p4 relation: a complete external-file setup with OPEN(ASYNCHRONOUS='YES'), one explicit ASYNCHRONOUS statement on a defined local output buffer, constant-YES transfer and a corresponding wait. That single explicit statement confirms the same-scope implicit attribute; the I/O implication is not a second explicit specification. Any run would check setup/initiation/completion errors, allow ID zero, avoid touching pending storage, and make no overlap/latency claim. Namelist-group-object and SIZE routes remain independently conditioned, not extra local S effects.
pending.use-host-block-source-identity: PENDING complete source/interface controls for a legitimate USE-associated variable, a host object and an enclosing nonlocal BLOCK object named only in an ASYNCHRONOUS statement. Preserve 14.2.2p2/p9/p10, 19.5.1.4 and 19.4; a type redeclaration or ALLOCATABLE statement can instead introduce a different object. Do not import VOLATILE's different coarray restrictions or propagate a BLOCK-only specification outside its scope.
pending.attribute-not-operation-source-gate: PENDING finite canonical relation to 8.5.4 S8.5.4-001/-002/-003, 12.6/12.7 and processor-qualified 18.10.4 communication. No declaration-only no-op, unchanged value print, compiler optimization outcome, MPI-looking call name or nonzero request ID proves the attribute effects or actual asynchrony. Entity-category or pending-affector violations need their own exact owners and diagnostic basis.

requirements.oracle: Compile/positive-controls and narrowly source-isolated grammar/reporting contrasts with minimal conforming repairs. The implicit-I/O and scope relationships need separately reviewed finite source/interface mechanisms; they are not implemented by this catalogue. Required reporting for a numbered syntax violation does not prescribe fatal rejection, a printed R834 or English wording.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Do not use two explicit specifications in one scope as a valid control; do not treat one explicit confirmation of the same-scope implicit I/O attribute as such a duplicate. ASYNCHRONOUS= in OPEN and a constant-YES data transfer have different roles. ID/IOSTAT/IOMSG are not added to the implicit attribute/pending-storage set merely because they are control variables. The processor may perform requested asynchronous I/O synchronously, and an unavailable feature, crash, resource error or unrelated diagnostic earns no grammar or execution credit.
